text:
Jack Hughes is shooting like a different player. He's at 1.63 expected goals per 60 minutes (a measure of the quality of chances he gets himself), up from 1.05 last season, and he has put 81 shots on goal while the Devils won eight of his last ten games. He has 27 points in 21 games, and the scoring isn't lucky: 10 goals on 11.79 expected, so if anything he has left a couple out there.

The bigger picture is that New Jersey controls the puck with him on the ice, 61.5% of the expected goals at five on five, and his last ten games brought 15 points against 12.4 expected. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking explains how: he carried the puck into the zone on 58% of his entries last season, and in tracked games carries led to a scoring chance 25% of the time, dump-ins 8%. Evolving-Hockey had him drawing more penalties than he takes, worth 2.2 goals. Our closest stylistic matches are Macklin Celebrini and Connor Bedard, which tells you where his game lives: on the puck, through the middle, at full speed.
